context:
Follow existing override pattern. For QSA4, mechanically replace
SUM(x) FILTER (WHERE cond) with sumIf(x, cond). For QTM1, wrap
order_time in toDateTime() before passing to toHour().
description:
6 query failures on ClickHouse in coffeeshop benchmark:
- QSA4 × 3: SUM(x) FILTER (WHERE cond) → ClickHouse needs sumIf(x, cond)
- QTM1 × 3: EXTRACT(HOUR FROM order_time) where order_time is TIME type →
  toHour() doesn't accept bare TIME values, needs toHour(toDateTime(order_time))

Part of Pattern B (EXTRACT) and Pattern D (FILTER aggregate).

anti_patterns.why: other platforms depend on standard SQL FILTER/EXTRACT

anti_patterns.dont: use toHour() directly on TIME columns
anti_patterns.why: ClickHouse toHour() rejects bare TIME values

preserves.behavior: Base coffeeshop QSA4/QTM1 queries unchanged - other platforms use standard FILTER and EXTRACT
Override queries return identical column names and semantics

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/ -v -k 'coffeeshop and clickhouse'
verifications.description: ClickHouse coffeeshop overrides load with sumIf and toDateTime wrappers
verifications.expected: Tests pass confirming sumIf/toDateTime overrides for QSA4/QTM1

work_units.summary: Create ClickHouse override for SA4 - actual issue is nested window aggregate SUM(SUM()) OVER (), replaced with CROSS JOIN subquery. TODO description was incorrect about FILTER clause.
Create ClickHouse override for TM1 using toHour(toDateTime(order_time)) for TIME-type column
Add unit tests: load SA4/TM1 for ClickHouse and assert SQL avoids nested window aggregate and uses toDateTime() respectively
